messages:
Priya Anand (AE): Heads-up: EdgeBridge just sent a detailed RFI. Key asks: capability matrix, POC pricing for 10-day trial, BYOM support for customer models on Private, explicit HSM/KMS wording, and how multi-region failover interacts with EU-only data residency. Can eng/security/contracts help?

Ethan Browne (SSE): I can pull the tech matrix. Clarify POC targets? concurrency, embed volume, model size?

Priya Anand (AE): They want to run a 10-day POC: 180 concurrent streams for gen, 40k embed calls/day, primary models ~16k context, occasional 32k for long-form. BYOM requirement: they want to host their fine-tuned model in their VPC and have Redwood route inference without model bits leaving their infra.

Hannah Wu (Eng-ML): BYOM on Private is supported via model deployment proxies and OCI-compatible image import. We should phrase carefully: "Private deployment option supports customer-hosted model artifacts in customer VPC; inference routing can be configured so model weights remain on customer infrastructure."

Sofia Martinez (Security): For HSM/KMS wording, approved line: "Customer-managed HSM or HSM-backed KMS supported for Private deployments; keys used for encryption and audit signing remain in customer-controlled hardware or vetted KMS; Redwood control plane never receives plaintext keys. Attestation and audit artifacts available under NDA." Legal to gate SOC2/ISO attachments.

Ethan Browne (SSE): Draft matrix snippet for the RFI table below. Need latency sanity-check for p50/p95 at 16k/32k.

Ethan Browne (SSE): ```
Feature | Hosted API | Dedicated (reserved) | Private (VPC / BYOM / HSM)
--- | --- | --- | ---
Context support | up to 32k (model dep) | up to 32k | up to 32k (BYOM models as-deployed)
Gen p50 (16k) | 140-230 ms | 90-150 ms | 95-170 ms
Gen p95 (16k) | 550-950 ms | 320-560 ms | 350-620 ms
Gen p50 (32k) | 450-700 ms | 300-450 ms | 320-500 ms
Embed p50 | 35-85 ms | 18-45 ms | 20-50 ms
Concurrent capacity | bursty to 100s | reserved 100-1k | configurable (customer pool)
Caching | automatic prefix/KV caching | tuned caching + reserved KV | local cache + KV in VPC
Quantization | bf16 / int8 | int8 recommended | custom quant + kernel tuning
BYOM | N/A | restricted | supported (Private only)
KMS / HSM | Redwood KMS | customer KMS integ | customer HSM (add-on), BYOK
SLA | standard | SLA-backed tiers | enterprise SLA
```

Hannah Wu (Eng-ML): Notes to include: p50/p95 ranges depend on model family and quant. For BYOM, performance can vary; recommend a short pre-POC perf calibration run. Also mention fallback rules: for strict EU-only tenancy, failover routing is limited to EU regions; for global failover we can route to nearest compatible region with customer consent.

Sofia Martinez (Security): Important: phrase EU-only tenancy clearly: "Dedicated and Private can be pinned to EU-only tenancy. Hosted API can be region-restricted to EU regions but not air-gapped; fallback to non-EU regions will not occur under EU-only tenancy unless customer provides explicit opt-in."

Ethan Browne (SSE): Pricing: rough 10-day POC estimates: hosted unoptimized ~$12k, optimized with caching/quant ~$4.5k; small dedicated 10-day reserved ~$21k; Private BYOM 10-day POC w/ HSM add-on starting ~$38k + integration (~$8k). I'll flag as preliminary.

Priya Anand (AE): Contracts/contracts-bot: can you confirm whether BYOM changes our standard POC contract language or adds indemnity clauses?

contracts-bot: Automated note: BYOM / customer-hosted artifacts require the BYOM addendum; additional clauses include model IP residency, liability carve-outs for customer-supplied artifacts, and a short technical attestation appendix. Legal review required.

Sofia Martinez (Security): Also add: for BYOM we require a short security checklist run (network ACLs, auth certs, image attestations) before routing production traffic. I'll attach the checklist.

Ethan Browne (SSE): Ops blurb for RFI: "Requests prefer reserved customer pools for Private/Dedicated. Fallback options: (1) queue/backpressure; (2) route to EU-hosted compatible pool (if not pinned); (3) route to quantized variant per policy; (4) fail closed if EU-only tenancy and no capacity."

Hannah Wu (Eng-ML): Acceptance criteria suggestion for POC: gen p95 <= 700ms (16k baseline), embed p50 <= 70ms, sustain 180 concurrent with <3% error rate, and BYOM model must pass attestation & calibration.

Priya Anand (AE): Plan: Ethan will draft matrix + pricing table, Sofia finalizes security lines and checklist, Hannah drafts BYOM how-to and perf calibration steps, contracts-bot provides BYOM addendum pointer. Can we aim to send the assembled RFI package to EdgeBridge by EOD tomorrow?

Ethan Browne (SSE): Will post draft by 2pm CET.

Sofia Martinez (Security): Uploading checklist and approved HSM wording to Drive now.

contracts-bot: Uploaded: edgebridge_BYOM_addendum_v1.docx :paperclip:

Priya Anand (AE): Thanks team :raised_hands: — let's keep responses concise and flag any legal/finance blockers early.
